sections.h2: How Cabarrus County values and bills a house
sections.html:
Cabarrus appraises each parcel at market value on January 1. One bill then goes to the owner, combining the county rate with any city, town and fire district rates for the address. Current values date from January 1, 2024, and no flat percentage was applied to earlier assessments.

A parcel's value is built from the land, the building (type, age and physical traits) and extras such as garages, sheds, pools, fences and driveways. A structure still going up is valued by how complete it is on January 1, and that figure goes into the bill.

The ceiling in G.S. 105-286 is eight years between reappraisals. Cabarrus halved that interval, so values track the market more closely.

sections.h2: Who to contact about assessments and appeals
sections.html:
The Tax Administration department handles assessment and appeals, and the Revaluation office answers value questions at 704-920-2126 or revalinfo@cabarruscounty.us. Visit 65 Church Street S in Concord, NC 28025, any weekday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

Collections bills on behalf of the county, seven cities or towns and 16 fire districts. The Equalization and Review Board takes appeals; the County Commissioners appoint its members from residents who know the local market.

  • Values and property cards: search online by owner name, address or parcel
  • Comparable sales: use the map tool on the Tax Revaluation page
  • Relief: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker, along with present use value and wildlife conservation
  • Payment plans: ask Collections

sections.h2: How to appeal your Cabarrus County value
sections.html:
Begin with a written request for informal review. You do not need a special form, but attached evidence strengthens the case. The appraiser covering your area reviews what you send and replies with an Informal Review notice that also explains how to move to the formal level.

From the date of that notice you have 30 days to carry the appeal forward. To ask for a hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review, write to Cabarrus County Tax Revaluation, PO Box 707, Concord, NC 28026-0707, or file through the county's online system. The assessor's office must receive it within 30 days of the date printed on your Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value, or at any point before the Board adjourns. Adjournment usually comes in late April, and the local newspaper carries the date.

Once you submit, you and the county appraiser get one more look at the case, and you fill out an Application for Hearing. The board listens to both sides, and its decision letter follows by mail within a month of the hearing. A disagreement that survives the board goes to the NC Property Tax Commission. G.S. 105-290 requires a written notice of appeal with your grounds, filed 30 days or less after the ruling was mailed.

The county does not accept a large increase from one revaluation to the next as grounds. Build your case from comparable sales.

Payment is due September 1. Once January 5 of the next year goes by, an unpaid bill is delinquent. Mailing happens once a year, in late July or the first days of August, for real estate, business and personal property alike.

A year on the Cabarrus County tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
January 1Parcels are valued, and the owner on this date gets the bill
JanuaryListing form for personal property opens, and real estate changes go on it
Late AprilReview board usually wraps up
By June 30Rates fixed through the budget
Late July to early AugustBills mailed
September 1Taxes due
After January 5Delinquent, so collection or foreclosure can follow

The interest rule in G.S. 105-360 adds 2 percent from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for every month that follows. A delinquent bill can lead to collection actions or tax foreclosure. A payment plan is available from Collections if you ask for it, ideally early in the year, yet the whole bill must still be paid by the delinquent date.

For 2026 the county charges $0.576 per $100 of assessed value. Cities, towns and fire districts layer their own rates over that, and an address inside Kannapolis, for instance, picks up another $0.5595.

Budget season produces the rates: the Board of Commissioners and each municipality finish theirs by June 30. A new assessed value does not by itself tell you what the bill will do, because that depends on the rates. For your own estimate, take the assessed value from the real estate search, add up the rates for every district covering the parcel, and have Collections check the result.

sections.h2: Tax breaks for Cabarrus County homeowners
sections.html:
Cabarrus has three relief programs on the county's list: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker. You pick only one, and the application form, AV-9, goes to the county assessor by June 1 ahead of the tax year. Present use value for farm, forest and wildlife land is handled separately with its own applications.

  • Homestead (G.S. 105-277.1): open to an owner at least 65, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is below $38,800 for 2026. The county leaves out $25,000 of value or half the appraisal, whichever is more.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value drops out of the bill. The state form sets no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: after five years in the home, your tax is held to 4.0% of income, or to 5.0% if income lands above the cap but no higher than $58,200 for 2026. Savings are deferred and secured by a lien.

sections.h2: Who pays the bill when you sell
sections.html:
Settle this year's bill out of your sale proceeds, which is what G.S. 105-355 contemplates. Billing follows ownership on the first of January, so a seller who closes mid-year should forward the bill to the buyer.

Owner-occupied homes in the county have a median value of $354,800, and 71.2 percent are lived in by their owners. The real estate search shows values set as of January 1, 2024, so look at recent neighborhood sales before you list. Your closing attorney should get a payoff for all taxes due, fire district amounts included. Ask Collections whether any earlier year is delinquent.

Pull your property card from the real estate search and check the land, building and extras the county has on file. Look at the comparable sales tool to see how nearby homes sold. Ask Collections for the current year's balance and any prior-year delinquency. If you receive homestead or circuit breaker relief, tell your closing attorney, since a deferral can come due. Last, confirm which bill goes to the buyer after closing, because the county issues it to whoever owned the parcel on January 1.

faqs.q: When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. A bill is past due if not paid before the following January 5, and state law starts interest on January 6. Bills are mailed in late July or the first days of August.

faqs.q: How often does Cabarrus County revalue real estate?
faqs.a: Every four years by local choice, although state law only requires every eight. The current values are as of January 1, 2024. The Revaluation office at 704-920-2126 can confirm the next cycle.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cabarrus County property value?
faqs.a: Submit a written request for an informal review, then appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review within 30 days of your value notice or before the board adjourns, usually in late April. The decision letter arrives within 30 days of the hearing.

faqs.q: Does Cabarrus County allow installments on a tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collections office works with taxpayers on payment plans, but you must request one and the bill still has to be paid in full by the delinquent date. Contacting them early in the year is preferred.

faqs.q: Who gets the bill if my Cabarrus County house sells before year end?
faqs.a: The bill still goes out in the name of the owner on January 1, so forward it to the buyer if you receive it after closing. Settle the current year's tax through closing so it does not turn into a lien problem for the new owner.
